methodology: The study used solid tellurite fibers fabricated via a stack-and-draw process to investigate their potential for broadband mid-IR supercontinuum generation. The dispersion and hydroxyl content of the fibers were characterized to optimize performance.
research_objective: To demonstrate solid tellurite fibers fabricated by the stack-and-draw method and investigate their suitability for broadband mid-IR supercontinuum generation, with a focus on optimizing fiber properties such as low dispersion and minimal residual OH.

key_findings.finding: Low dispersion and low residual OH content are beneficial for broadband mid-IR supercontinuum generation in tellurite fibers.
Novel stack-and-draw process for fabricating solid tellurite optical fibers without an outer tube, demonstrating a simple and flexible fabrication method with reduced risk of contamination.

Demonstrated all-solid tellurite fibers with this new stack-and-draw process and MIR supercontinuum generation in these tellurite fibers pumped by Tm-doped fiber lasers, identifying optimal fiber designs for efficient broadband MIR supercontinuum generation.
Optimized design of the fiber based on refractive index data and fiber dispersion simulation.
The minimum achievable ZDW is 2.21 µm with the current refractive index contrast between core and cladding.
